---
title: "CONSORT diagrams"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.align = "center")
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(cohortflow)

dat <- mock_parallel_rct(n_participants = 300, seed = 2024)
```

`as_consort_diagram()` draws a CONSORT-style flow diagram from a `cf_flow`.
It is built from the same attrition tibble as `as_attrition_table()`, so the
numbers in the diagram and the table always match. The result is a ggplot,
so it prints anywhere a plot does and can be saved at publication quality
with `save_consort_diagram()`.

## Reading the diagram

```{r, fig.width = 5.9, fig.height = 3.8, fig.alt = "Linear CONSORT diagram: 300 assessed; an Age box with 279 after listing two age exclusion reasons; then Passed screening 253 and Consented 226."}
crit <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ !is.na(age), label = "Age recorded", reason = "Age missing", category = "Age") |>
  include(~ age >= 18, label = "Aged 18 or over", reason = "Under 18", category = "Age") |>
  include(~ eligible_screen, label = "Passed screening", reason = "Failed screening") |>
  include(~ !is.na(consent_date), label = "Consented", reason = "Did not consent")

flow <- apply_criteria(dat, crit, id = "participant_id")
as_consort_diagram(flow)
```

- The top box is everyone assessed (`assessed_label`).
- Each main box below it is a step, or a category of consecutive steps,
  showing **how many remain after it**.
- The side box on the arrow into a main box shows **how many that step
  removed**, as a count and a percentage of those entering it. For a
  category, the box lists each step's own count.
- The last box is the final cohort (`final_label`).

`show_categories = FALSE` draws every step as its own box.

### Which text goes in which box

Each number sits beside text that describes those people, so a box never
says "Withdrew consent (n=226)" about the people who stayed:

| Step | Main box (number remaining) | Side box (number removed) |
|---|---|---|
| `include(~ age >= 18, "Aged 18 or over", reason = "Under 18")` | Aged 18 or over | Under 18 |
| `include()` with no `reason` | its label | Excluded |
| `exclude(~ withdrew, "Withdrew consent")` | Remaining (`remaining_label`) | Withdrew consent |
| Steps sharing a `category` | the category | each step's `reason`, listed |

An inclusion step's label says who is **kept**, so give it a `reason` that
says who is **removed**. Inside a category the reasons are listed, and a step
without one would be listed under its label ("Aged 18 or over (n=6)" for six
people under 18). `as_consort_diagram()` warns when that happens.

## Styling

The defaults suit journal submission: black outlines, no fill, 9-point text.
Every element can be changed:

```{r, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 4.9, fig.alt = "The same diagram with a title, teal outlines, pale fills and wrapped labels."}
as_consort_diagram(
  flow,
  title = "Participant flow",
  main_fill = "#E6F2F1",
  excl_fill = "#FFF4E5",
  border_colour = "#0B6E69",
  border_linewidth = 0.4,
  text_size = 10,
  wrap_width = 26,
  assessed_label = "Referred to the study",
  final_label = "Eligible and consented"
)
```

| Argument | Controls |
|---|---|
| `main_fill`, `excl_fill` | Fill of the main and side boxes (default none) |
| `border_colour`, `border_linewidth` | Box outlines and arrows |
| `text_size`, `text_colour`, `font_family` | Box text |
| `title`, `title_colour` | Optional title above the diagram |
| `wrap_width` | Wrap long labels at this many characters |
| `digits`, `big_mark` | Percentage decimals and the thousands separator (`"1,234"`) |
| `arrow_size` | Arrowhead length, in inches |

Because the diagram is a ggplot, ggplot2 layers and themes can be added:

```{r, fig.width = 5.9, fig.height = 4.1, fig.alt = "The default diagram with a caption added underneath."}
as_consort_diagram(flow) +
  ggplot2::labs(caption = "Synthetic data from mock_parallel_rct().")
```

## Randomised trials

Add a `randomise()` step and the diagram splits there. Everything before it
is one shared trunk. At the randomisation box it divides into one column
per arm, and every later step is counted separately within each arm, which
is how CONSORT asks for post-allocation losses to be reported.

```{r, fig.width = 10.2, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "CONSORT diagram that splits after the Randomised box into Control and Intervention columns, each with its own withdrawal and baseline exclusions."}
crit_rct <- crit |>
  randomise(by = "participant_id", arms = "arm") |>
  exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew consent") |>
  include(~ baseline_complete, label = "Baseline complete", reason = "Baseline incomplete")

flow_rct <- apply_criteria(dat, crit_rct, id = "participant_id")
as_consort_diagram(flow_rct)
```

The arm column comes from the `arms` argument of `randomise()`. To split on
a different column, pass `branch_by`.

## Splitting without a randomisation step

Without `randomise()`, `branch_by` splits the final cohort into one box per
value of a column. That suits a cohort study reported by exposure group, or
a trial whose allocation happened before the data begins:

```{r, fig.width = 6.3, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Linear diagram ending in a final cohort box that splits into Control and Intervention boxes."}
as_consort_diagram(flow, branch_by = "arm", final_label = "Allocated")
```

Rows where the `branch_by` column is `NA` get their own box, labelled by
`branch_na_label`.

## Crossover trials

In a crossover trial every participant receives each treatment in turn.
`stage_by` adds one box per period beneath each sequence, and
`stage_label_by` labels each period with the treatment given in it. Each
participant has one row per period, so `count_by` makes every box count
participants. It names a level of the flow's hierarchy, so the flow is built
with `hierarchy =`:

```{r, fig.width = 5.8, fig.height = 5.4, fig.alt = "Crossover CONSORT diagram: after randomisation the AB and BA sequences each show period boxes for treatments A then B, or B then A."}
co <- mock_crossover(n_participants = 120, seed = 11)

flow_co <- apply_criteria(
  co,
  cf_criteria() |>
    include(~ eligible_screen, label = "Passed screening", reason = "Failed screening") |>
    include(~ !is.na(consent_date), label = "Consented", reason = "Did not consent") |>
    exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew"),
  id = "event_id",
  hierarchy = cf_hierarchy(participant = "participant_id")
)

as_consort_diagram(
  flow_co,
  branch_by = "sequence",
  stage_by = "period",
  stage_label_by = "arm",
  count_by = "participant_id",
  final_label = "Randomised"
)
```

The trunk, sequence and period boxes all count people, so they add up. A
participant counts as removed at the step where they lose their last
period. Without `count_by`, every box would count participant-periods (two
per person).

## Saving for publication

`save_consort_diagram()` writes PNG, TIFF, JPEG, PDF, SVG or EPS, choosing
the format from the file extension. By default the page is sized from the
diagram's layout so the text fits its boxes, at 300 dpi for raster formats:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
diagram <- as_consort_diagram(flow_rct)

save_consort_diagram(diagram, "figure1.pdf")             # vector, fonts embedded
save_consort_diagram(diagram, "figure1.tiff", dpi = 600) # many journals want TIFF
save_consort_diagram(diagram, "figure1.svg")             # editable in Inkscape/Illustrator
save_consort_diagram(flow_rct, "figure1.png")            # a flow works too, with default styling
```

Give only `width` (or only `height`) to fix one dimension and keep the
aspect ratio. Text is always drawn at `text_size` points, so to fit a wide
diagram, such as a two-arm trial, into a single journal column, build it
with a smaller `text_size` rather than shrinking the page:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
small <- as_consort_diagram(flow_rct, text_size = 7)
save_consort_diagram(small, "figure1-column.pdf")
```

In R Markdown or Quarto, print the diagram in a chunk and set `fig-width`
and `fig-height` to roughly the size `save_consort_diagram()` would choose.

## Under the hood

The box and arrow positions are attached to the diagram, in case you want
to draw it some other way or check the layout:

```{r}
layout <- attr(as_consort_diagram(flow_rct), "consort_layout")
names(layout)
head(layout$main_boxes[, c("label", "x", "y", "w", "h")])
```
